newsitem.title: UK: UK's ECGD had sharp rise in business in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: UK's ECGD had sharp rise in business in 1995/96.

text.p: The Export Credits Guarantee Department (ECGD) on Thursday said its financial position was the healthiest since the world debt crisis.

"1995/96 was an excellent year for UK project exporters. This was reflected in the high value of guarantees issued by the ECGD, almost equalling our post-world debt crisis record of 4.08 billion stg," chief executive Brian Willott told reporters.
This year it was able to contribute 246 million stg to the UK Treasury after several years of deficit or very small surpluses.

"With the continued substantial decline in claims and a sharp rise in recoveries, ECGD's accounts are now the healthiest they have been since the start of the debt crisis in the early 1980s," Willott said.

Guarantees issued for new business rose 35 percent from last year to 4.6 billion stg, while the trading surplus on its new business account rose to 103.3 million stg from 60.0 million. Premium income was up to 156.5 million stg from 112.5 million.
Recoveries from rescheduled debt were 473.2 million stg, compared with 341.1 million.
The ECGD's top markets for new business in 1995/96 were China -- for the second year in a row -- followed by Indonesia, the Philippines and Turkey.
China is also where the ECGD has the most exposure. Nigeria was in second place but most of that is in Paris Club debt.
The dominance of Asia was due largely to two power projects -- Ling Ao in China and Sual in the Philippines.
Willott doubted China business would be quite as large in the coming year.
He noted that 60 percent of its business was in the civil sector, exceeding aerospace and defence combined, which was the more normal pattern.
In the past three years, defence and aerospace have accounted for at least half of total capital goods and project business.
